summary: 3 confirmed findings: 1 Medium, 2 Low, 0 High, 0 Critical. 3 fixed and retested; 0 open or unverified. 5 service hosts inventoried. The latest unauthenticated Nuclei pass produced 20 informational template matches; these are observations, not automatically confirmed vulnerabilities.

findings.title: SMB signing is optional
findings.risk: A malicious peer on office-lan could tamper with unsigned SMB sessions or participate in relay attacks. Requires access to this local lab network; no internet exposure was observed.
findings.remediation: Set server signing = mandatory in the persistent fileserver Compose command; recreate the service and require signed client sessions.
findings.verification: Compare the baseline Nmap smb2-security-mode (enabled but not required) with a direct SMB2 NEGOTIATE response on host loopback 1445 and the retest Nmap output (required). Confirm alice can still list Finance with signing required. In this Samba client, signing=disabled remains a preference and does not force an unsigned session when the server requires signing; its exit code is not a closure criterion.
findings.rating: CVSS-style qualitative Medium: adjacent-network prerequisite, potential confidentiality/integrity impact. No exploit chain or numeric CVSS score asserted.

findings.title: Zero minimum password age permits rapid password changes
findings.risk: An authenticated fictional user can change passwords repeatedly, reducing the value of the 12-password history. No weak password or completed history bypass is claimed.
findings.remediation: Set minimum password age to one day in seed.sh and the running directory; preserve administrative password-reset workflows.
findings.verification: Create one temporary fictional assessment_probe account with random strong passwords. Perform two self-service changes, then remove the account in finally. Retest must reject an immediate self-service change.
findings.rating: CVSS-style qualitative Low: requires a valid local domain account; policy weakness without demonstrated compromise.

findings.asset: wg-easy, Uptime Kuma, CUPS / host loopback
findings.title: Administration uses plaintext HTTP
findings.risk: Admin sessions and CUPS Basic credentials lack transport encryption on the host-facing HTTP listeners. Loopback binding substantially reduces exposure; privileged host compromise is outside this proof.
findings.remediation: Terminate TLS with a local Caddy CA on the same loopback admin ports and remove direct HTTP host publications. Trust the exported public CA explicitly. Internal office-lan HTTP remains a documented residual risk.
findings.verification: Make credential-free HTTP requests to all three original ports before remediation, then verify HTTP no longer serves the application and HTTPS validates against the exported lab CA.
findings.rating: CVSS-style qualitative Low in this loopback-only deployment. Three endpoints are grouped under one root cause; not three inflated findings.
